title: Someone Spammed My DEV Post. I Traced It to a Wombat.
why_read: An entertaining and well-documented investigative writeup tracing a spam comment through a redirect chain to a legitimate affiliate marketing operation, offering genuine insight into how low-effort spam economics work.
analysis: The author traces a spam comment on their Dev.to article through a chain of URL shorteners and throwaway domains, ultimately finding it leads to a real SaaS product with an affiliate code, not malware or a scam. They calculate that only three signups a year make the whole low-effort spam operation profitable, explaining why such comment spam persists despite platform moderation. This kind of hands-on investigative tracing, backed by a public GitHub repo with raw evidence and a reproduction script, offers a concrete look at internet economics and abuse vectors. It's a lightweight but genuinely interesting piece of applied security/OSINT analysis relevant to anyone running a blog or community platform.
